headline: Reproduction is life creating more life—the fundamental drive to continue beyond individual existence
universal_truth: Everything that persists has a way to reproduce itself; continuation requires creating the next generation
fun_facts: An octopus mother guards her eggs for months, starving herself, dying after they hatch
A single dandelion can produce 15,000 seeds that travel miles on the wind
Some bacteria reproduce every 20 minutes—one cell becomes a billion in 10 hours
discussion_questions: What do you want to reproduce beyond yourself—ideas, values, creations?
How do you ensure what you care about continues?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every living thing does one thing above all else: make more of itself. Oak trees make acorns. Bacteria divide. Animals have offspring. Life's deepest drive isn't survival—it's continuation beyond individual existence.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Reproduction seems obviously important, but what does life's universal drive to reproduce teach us more broadly?

options.text: Reproduction shows that lasting success means creating successors—individual survival is temporary; only what reproduces persists through time
options.response: Yes. Species that don't reproduce disappear. Ideas that don't spread die. Organizations that don't renew fade. Reproduction is the mechanism of persistence.
Instinct drives it, but the pattern applies beyond biology...

q1.title: Strategies Vary
q1.script: Some species produce millions of offspring with no care. Others produce few with intensive investment. Both strategies work in different contexts. How you reproduce matters as much as whether you do.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Strategies Vary"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Cost of Continuation
q2.script: Reproduction costs—energy, resources, sometimes life itself. The salmon dies after spawning. The octopus starves guarding eggs. Continuation beyond self requires investment, sometimes sacrifice.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Beyond Biology
q3.script: Humans reproduce ideas, skills, organizations, cultures. Teachers reproduce knowledge. Artists reproduce vision. Mentors reproduce capability. What you pass on is your broader reproduction.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Everything that persists has a way to reproduce itself. Continuation requires creating the next generation—of offspring, ideas, or impact.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 263. Tomorrow, we'll explore the code of life—DNA and genetics. Until then, consider what you want to reproduce beyond yourself.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Legacy Planning - What Do You Reproduce?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify what to pass on beyond yourself
growTrack.activity: What do you want to persist beyond your individual existence—children, ideas, values, skills, organizations? How are you actively reproducing these things? Legacy is reproductive success. What's your strategy?
